task.title: Recurrence sum: Lemma A's evaluation of the driving sum

located_defect.declaration: SE_cs_1957_a2388_Census.LocalClaimNat (Nat model; the real model SE_cs_1957_a2388_Census.LocalClaimReal is the same claim over ℝ)
located_defect.description: Lemma A of the source (stored source line 0053) evaluates the driving sum g(n) = sum_{j} a^j h(n / b^j) at n = b^L and asserts g(n) = n^{log_b a} (log_b n)^{k+1}. In the Nat model (a = b^p, n = b^L, Mathlib's Nat.log) this universal identity is the located defect. Supply the corrected right-hand side and prove the corrected identity for every b ≥ 2, p, k, L; there is no separate target theorem beyond the corrected statement.

task.allowed_edit: Replace the hole in `rhs` by an expression in b, p, k, L (a Finset sum over an explicit range in L is allowed; no reference to drivingSum, drivingSumAux, h, lgb, Nat.log, middleTerm, claimedRHS; no if/match); nothing else in the fixed part may change. The driving sum and the source's h, the power inputs n = b^L, a = b^p, and the quantification over all k and L are fixed; k or L may not be restricted. Do not redefine any declaration of defs_only; no instances, notations, macros, axioms or exports.
task.challenged_passage: 0053 $$g(n) = \displaystyle n^{\log_b a} \log_b^k n \; \sum_{j=0}^{\log_b{n-1}}  \left(\frac{a}{b^{\log_b a}}\right)^j = n^{\log_b a} \log_b^{k +1} n.$$

notes: Judgement call: the contract keeps two readings (Nat model, real model) and leaves the scored one to the runner. The Nat model is templated because its instances are kernel-decidable; the real model (Real.logb, rpow) is not templated: its instance checks would need Real.logb simplification lemmas whose success depends on the syntactic form of the solver's rhs (a fail-closed agreement test would then reject admissible answers).
Nonvacuity is existential (leak-free); the witness (2,1,1,2) is checked only in AGREE.lean.
The corrected value is a power sum with no closed form; the template therefore allows an explicit Finset sum in L and forbids only the driving sum's own vocabulary.
